title: Snake diet review
summary: Working from the official website, he critiques the snake diet (a 1-2 hour eating window plus electrolyte 'snake juice'). He agrees with some of its energy-balance points but calls it a marketed crash diet: impractical, bad for mood and sleep, built on an evolutionary appeal, and likely to end in rebound because it never teaches maintenance. His alternative is to swap processed food for vegetables and whole foods while training.
claims: Diets are tools; becoming emotionally attached to one damages your ability to judge it objectively and progress
The snake diet name is marketing: snakes do not eat once a day, and captive snakes eat far more often than wild ones
When a fitness or health practice becomes a money-making machine, question it, because it was likely built to make money rather than help you
A diet should never be a lifestyle (vegans get a pass for ethics); it should fit your needs and genetic predispositions, and habits should not define you
Snake juice is just water with minerals and salts, like a water fast; not dangerous
Fasting is not the only way to access fat stores; a recomp mobilises fat through training without a deficit
A diet that is not paired with a training regimen loses about half its potential to transform the body
In a deficit or fast the body prioritises burning fat over muscle because muscle is costly to build; it will not burn all fat first, but it favours fat
Crash diets fail at maintenance because they never teach calorie control, whole foods, or stopping when no longer hungry
Justifying a diet by evolution is the naturalistic fallacy
Exercise alone burns few calories, especially weight training, and diet alone does not sculpt the body; diet and training must go hand in hand
Everyone fasts overnight, so intermittent fasting just extends it; three meals a day is a cultural construct built around farm working hours
When you eat matters little compared with what and how much; meal distribution only affects how you get through the day
Even 5000 kcal is very hard to eat in a 1-2 hour window because satiety cuts you off
People who overeat usually eat very frequently or choose calorie-dense foods that do not satiate
Rapid weight loss tends to cause loose skin, cellular cleansing claims mean nothing, and starvation mode does not exist
A 1-2 hour eating window is impractical for anyone with a demanding job; going to bed hungry hurts sleep and next-day performance
Fasting puts many people, especially the overweight, in a dark place: sad, depressed or aggressive
Ancestors strove for consistent food supplies; blame the person who shops five times a week, not the 24/7 supermarket; the diet removes personal responsibility
Losing a lot of weight fast and then regaining it is worse for metabolism and organs than staying fat; he opposes crash bulks and cuts but accepts slow cuts, slow bulks and recomps
Giving people with an unhealthy relationship to food a 2-hour window invites binging, usually on junk; a calorie is not just a calorie if it all comes from junk
Fasting is not magic and will not boost testosterone
Instead of crash diets, replace processed foods with vegetables and whole foods; calories fall on their own because fibre-rich food is more satiating
Training matters more than diet for naturals; this is not a diet channel
